title: Moving Charges and Magnetism
seo_title: Moving Charges and Magnetism Class 12 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 4)
standard_code: Class 12 Physics, Chapter 4: Moving Charges and Magnetism
standard_text: Concept of magnetic field, Oersted's experiment. Biot–Savart law and its application to current carrying circular loop. Ampere's law and its applications to infinitely long straight wire, straight solenoid (only qualitative treatment), force on a moving charge in uniform magnetic and electric fields. Force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field, force between two parallel current-carrying conductors – definition of ampere, torque experienced by a current loop in uniform magnetic field; current loop as a magnetic dipole and its magnetic dipole moment, moving coil galvanometer – its current sensitivity and conversion to ammeter and voltmeter.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 4 Moving Charges and Magnetism: magnetic force on charges and wires, fields of wires, loops and solenoids, the cyclotron, parallel currents and the galvanometer. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: F = qvB sin θ; F = BIl sin θ.
body_html:
How to think about it

A magnetic field exerts a force qvB sin θ on a moving charge, at right angles to its velocity, so the charge moves in a circle of radius mv/qB and does no work. A wire in a field feels F = BIl sin θ. Currents make fields: μ₀I/2πr round a long wire, μ₀NI/2R at the centre of a loop and μ₀nI inside a solenoid.

Parallel currents in the same direction attract. A current loop is a magnetic dipole with m = NIA. A galvanometer becomes an ammeter with a small shunt in parallel and a voltmeter with a large resistance in series.

Example

5 A, 0.1 m from a long wire?

2 × 10⁻⁷ × 5 ÷ 0.1

Answer: 10⁻⁵ T

Example

Galvanometer to voltmeter?

series

Answer: large resistance in series

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a magnetic field speeds up a charge.
  • Using μ₀I/2R for a long wire.
  • Putting the shunt in series.

faq.q: Why does a magnetic field do no work on a moving charge?
faq.a: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so the speed does not change.

faq.q: How is a galvanometer made into an ammeter?
faq.a: By connecting a small shunt resistance in parallel so most of the current bypasses the coil.

items.q: A proton moves at 2,000,000 m/s at right angles to a 0.01 T magnetic field. Calculate the radius of its circular path.
items.e: BQv = mv²/r, so r = mv/(BQ) = 2.09 m.

items.q: What is the cyclotron frequency for protons in a magnetic field of 1.7 T? (q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg)
items.e: f = qB/(2πm) = 2.59 × 107 Hz (it does not depend on speed).

items.q: What is the Lorentz force?
c: the total force qE + q(v × B) on a moving charge
items.e: It combines electric and magnetic forces.
